368869.title: Zhao's bipartite swapping conjecture
368869.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph and let $q\geq 2$. Write $K_q$ for the complete graph on $q$ vertices, and let $H\times K_2$ denote the categorical product with the two-vertex complete graph. **Zhao's bipartite swapping conjecture.**

$$
\hom(H,K_q)^2 \leq \hom(H\times K_2,K_q).
$$

This inequality is a proposed bipartite-swapping property for proper $q$-colourings. The paper states that it remains unknown in general, although it is proved for several classes of graphs later in the paper.

368976.title: The Feynman-period characterization of Speyer's invariant
368976.statement:
A graph is **cyclically $6$-connected** if it is $4$-regular and has no $4$-edge cut other than one isolating a vertex; cyclically $4$-connected $3$-regular graphs are defined analogously. For such a graph $G$, let $\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}(G)$ denote its Feynman period after deleting any vertex, and let $\mathsf{N}_2(G)$ be the second Speyer invariant.

**Period--Speyer conjecture.** If two cyclically $6$-connected $4$-regular graphs, or two cyclically $4$-connected $3$-regular graphs, satisfy

$$
\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}(G_1)=\widetilde{\mathcal{P}}(G_2),
$$

then

$$
\mathsf{N}_2(G_1)=\mathsf{N}_2(G_2).
$$

This would make $\mathsf{N}_2$ a function of the Feynman period on these graph classes. It is supported by all graphs with known periods but remains open.

369233.title: The three-sevenths upper-bound conjecture for the game isolation number
369233.statement:

369271.title: Räty–Sudakov–Tomon surplus conjecture for graphs far from clique unions
369271.statement:
Let $G$ be a regular graph on $n$ vertices, with max-cut surplus $\mathsf{sp}(G)$. Say that $G$ is **$epsilon$-far** from a graph $H$ if no graph isomorphic to $H$ can be obtained from $G$ by adding or removing at most $epsilon |V(G)|^2$ edges.

**Räty–Sudakov–Tomon conjecture.** For any $epsilon>0$, there exists a $c>0$ such that, if $G$ is $epsilon$-far from every disjoint union of cliques, then

$$
\mathsf{sp}(G) geq c n^{5/4}.
$$

This conjecture predicts a polynomial improvement over Edwards' bound for regular graphs that are far from the natural low-surplus examples. The supplied text gives no resolution; the cited work establishes a related lower bound with a logarithmic loss in a restricted very dense regular setting.

369354.title: DeBiasio–Han–Lo–Molla–Piga–Treglown conjecture on Turánable oriented graphs
369354.statement:

369359.title: Equitable full-cookie distribution conjecture
369359.statement:
Let $r$, $n$, and $m$ be positive integers. A group of $r$ children has $n$ cookies, each with some amount of one or more of $m$ possible kinds of frosting.

**Equitable distribution conjecture.** It should be possible to cut at most $(r-1)m$ cookies and distribute them so that each child has the same amount of each kind of frosting and at least

$$
\left\lfloor \frac{n-m(r-1)}{r}\right\rfloor
$$

full cookies.

The bound would be optimal because an equitable distribution of all full cookies can give each child at most $\left\lfloor\frac{n-m(r-1)}{r}\right\rfloor$ full cookies. The conjecture strengthens the paper's theorem by improving its guaranteed number of full cookies while retaining the optimal cut bound.

369576.title: Frankl's conjecture on shattering in antichains
369576.statement:
Let $2^{[n]}$ denote the family of all subsets of $[n]$. A family $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is an **antichain** if no two members satisfy $F\subseteq F'$.

**Frankl's conjecture.** Let $k$ be a non-negative integer and $n\geqslant 2k$. If $\mathcal{F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$ is an antichain with $\mathcal{F}\not\rightarrow(k+1,2^{k+1})$, then

$$
|\mathcal{F}|\leqslant\binom{n}{k}.
$$

Frankl proved the conjecture for $k\leqslant 2$, and Anstee and Sali proved it for $k=3$; the general case remains open.

369934.title: Dewdney's circuit-and-enumeration conjecture for (m,n)-trees
369934.statement:
Let $n\geq 1$, let $0\leq m\leq n-1$, and let $K$ be a pure $n$-simplicial complex. $$
\alpha_k(K)=\frac{\alpha_0(K)-m-1}{n-m}\binom{n+1}{k+1}-\frac{\alpha_0(K)-n-1}{n-m}\binom{m+1}{k+1}.
$$

Dewdney posed this as an unresolved structural characterisation of $(m,n)$-trees; the source does not report a resolution.

369971.title: Convergence conjecture for the Temperley–Lieb algebra rewriting system
369971.statement:
Let $n$ be the rank parameter of the presented Temperley–Lieb algebra, with generators $\delta,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1}$. Consider the rewriting system on words in $\{\delta,e_1,\dots,e_{n-1}\}$ whose rules are

$$
e_i\delta\to\delta e_i,\qquad e_i^2\to\delta e_i,
$$

$$
e_i e_{i\pm1}e_i\to e_i,\qquad e_i e_j\to e_j e_i\text{ if }j<i-1.
$$

**Convergence conjecture.** This rewriting system is convergent, meaning that it is terminating and confluent.

If true, every word has a unique normal form, yielding an algorithm for reducing words and thereby solving equality in the presented Temperley–Lieb algebra.
